summary: Trout Creek Butte's 1933 steel Aermotor lookout, 86 feet tall, was on standby from 1972, burned on its summit in 2017, and is closed to climbing.

facts.design: 86-foot steel Aermotor tower with 7 by 7 foot cab
facts.status_note: Register says on standby since 1972. A May 2020 visit listed it as abandoned, with the cabin floor gone, the summit burned in 2017, and a climbing warning on the tower.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Sisters Ranger District

access.note: Not open to climbing. A 2020 visitor reported an inspection tag warning people not to climb, and the lower stairs had been removed.

visit.trail_note: In May 2020 the road up was in good shape and passable by any vehicle. No source read says the public may climb the tower.

events.note: Steel Aermotor tower erected in August 1933, with help from a 20-man CCC crew. Height given as 75 ft in planning notices, 80 ft in an August 1933 newspaper item and 86 ft by the Register and firelookout.com.
14-by-16-foot wood frame cabin built for living quarters.
Paul Tallone named lookout foreman for the summer.
Flare-up in timber on the southeast side of Black Crater, spotted from the lookout at 11 p.m.; a crew was sent at 3 a.m. Reported in a July 17, 1935 item.
Dick Compton on duty as lookout.
Gordon Landdon, who had staffed the lookout through the fire season, closed it in September 1940.
Carl Demoy took his station as forest service lookout in July 1948.
Placed on standby status, per the Register.
Milli Fire burned much of the summit; some trees right by the lookout survived.
May 2020 visit: status abandoned, cabin floor gone, roof largely gone, lower stairs removed, inspection tag warning against climbing.

corrections.why: 22.9 m is 75 feet, the figure from the 1932-33 planning notices and the Oregon Lookouts 1933 entry. The Register, firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill all give 86 feet, which is 26.2 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Planning notices and the Oregon Lookouts 1933 entry give 75 feet. An August 1933 newspaper item gives 80 feet. The Register, firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 86 feet. The record uses 86 feet as the figure that matches the current structure in all three recent sources.
The Register gives 5,438 ft (1,658 m). firelookout.com and Cheryl Hill give 5,546 ft. The brief's 1,657.5 m matches the Register, and the record keeps the Register figure.

The Register says on standby since 1972; firelookout.com says last used for emergencies in the 1970s; Cheryl Hill lists it as abandoned in 2020. The record keeps status as standing and records the conflict in status_note.

notes_for_editor: Height is the main correction: the brief's 22.9 m is the 75-foot planning figure, and three sources give 86 feet. The Register's comments on bullet holes and paint are undated. The NHLR staffing field (no) is undated, so staffing rests mainly on the 2020 visit. The Oregon Lookouts history was read to 1958 and then 1992 (an outhouse move); the 1960s-1980s history is not covered. The Milli Fire date and summit burn come from Cheryl Hill only; a search result for a Sisters-area Nugget article describing a mosaic burn was not read and is not cited. A 1991 Forest Service eligibility report for Deschutes lookouts appears in the Oregon State Library collection but was not read. No photos added: the Forest Fire Lookout Association post and the museum photo credit lack image URLs that were read.
